column2: Moses reports everything commanded, retaining this sentence at the selected chapter opening rather than shifting the numbering.
The tribal rulers receive the Lord's word through Moses; the two levels of speech remain distinct.
Vow, oath and self-imposed restriction all bind the speaker; profaning his word is prohibited and the whole spoken commitment must be done.
The young woman's vow or restriction is situated in her father's house, a condition continued in the following verses.
A father's hearing and silence leave every vow and restriction standing; neither hearing nor repeated universality is dropped.
Refusal must occur on the day of hearing. The Lord cleanses her because her father refused, preserving the selected cleansing verb.
Marriage occurs while earlier vows remain upon her. The specific declaration of her lips is retained without importing rashness.
The husband's silence on the day he hears confirms all vows and restrictions, matching the repeated temporal condition.
Same-day refusal leaves none of the obligations in force, and the Lord cleanses her; the husband's refusal remains the expressed reason.
A widow's or divorced woman's self-directed vow remains binding; against her conveys the obligation, not a new accusation.
A vow made in her husband's house or an oath-bound restriction introduces the next conditional case.
Hearing, silence and absence of refusal all remain; the repeated standing of vows and restrictions is preserved.
Utter annulment on the day of hearing cancels what came from her lips; the husband annuls and the Lord cleanses.
Every vow and self-afflicting oath is subject to establishment or annulment by her husband; both alternatives remain.
Continued silence confirms the obligations because he was silent on the hearing day, preserving the explanatory clause.
Late annulment makes the husband bear his sin. The selected masculine possessive is not harmonized to her sin.
The concluding ordinances cover husband and wife, and father and youthful daughter in his house; both relationships remain.
The Lord's speech to Moses introduces the vengeance command.
Vengeance concerns Israel and Midian, followed by Moses being gathered to his people; the order remains explicit.
The warriors fight before the Lord and repay Midian with vengeance from the Lord. The repeated divine relationship is retained.
One thousand from each tribe, from all Israel's tribes, is the specified levy for battle.
Twelve thousand equipped warriors result from the thousand-per-tribe count; neither quantity is generalized.
Phinehas is identified through Eleazar and Aaron, and sacred vessels and signalling trumpets remain in their plural hands.
The battle follows the Lord's command to Moses and kills every male, without softening the stated scope.
The five kings remain Evi, Zur, Rekem, Hur and Robok in selected order; Balaam son of Beor is separately killed by sword with the slain.
Women, dependents, livestock, possessions and resources are distinguished in the taking and plundering.
column3: The context supports dependents for the collective household term here; its range is not settled for every other occurrence.

column2: Both settlement towns and farmsteads are burned, retaining the paired objects and explicit fire.
All plunder and spoils span people through livestock; the sentence continues into their delivery.
Captives, spoils and plunder reach Moses, Eleazar and all Israel at Araboth Moab on the Jordan opposite Jericho.
Moses, Eleazar and all congregation rulers meet the returning force outside the camp.
Moses' anger addresses the returning officers, with commanders of thousands and hundreds both specified.
His question challenges the preservation of every female alive, retaining the interrogative form.
Balaam's word, the women's causation, Israel's disregard of the Lord's word, Peor and the plague remain linked as stated.
The command includes every male dependent and women who have known a male's bed; its violence is neither omitted nor intensified.
Female dependents who have not known a male's bed are to be kept alive. The selected text does not add for yourselves.
Seven days outside camp and purification on days three and seven apply to killers and corpse-touchers, both soldiers and captives.
Coverings, leather, goats' hair articles and wood all receive purification; the four material classes remain.
Eleazar addresses the returning warriors with the law's ordinance prescribed to Moses by the Lord.
The metals remain gold, silver, bronze, iron, lead and tin, preserving the selected lead-before-tin sequence.
Fire-resistant objects still require purification water; objects not passing through fire pass through water, without an invented procedure.
Washing clothes on day seven precedes cleansing and re-entry into camp.
A new speech from the Lord introduces the distribution rules.
Moses, Eleazar and ancestral-house rulers count all captive spoil, human through livestock.
The spoil is divided between warriors and the whole congregation; the ensuing halves explain the distribution.
The warriors' levy is one in five hundred. The selected list includes people, livestock, cattle, sheep and goats, without replacing goats with donkeys.
The levy comes from the warriors' half and goes to Eleazar as the Lord's firstfruits.
The congregation's half yields one in fifty for the Levites; people, cattle, sheep, donkeys and all livestock remain in the list.
Moses and Eleazar carry out the Lord's prescription to Moses.
The sheep total is six hundred seventy-five thousand, beginning the itemized surplus rather than a rounded estimate.
Seventy-two thousand cattle are retained as the second total.
Sixty-one thousand donkeys are retained as the third total.
Thirty-two thousand human beings are specifically women who have not known a man's bed.
The warriors' sheep half is three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred, exactly half the stated total.
Six hundred seventy-five sheep are the Lord's levy, one five-hundredth of the warriors' half.
Thirty-six thousand cattle form the warriors' half, and seventy-two the one-in-five-hundred levy.
Thirty thousand five hundred donkeys form the warriors' half, and sixty-one the levy.
Sixteen thousand human beings form the warriors' half, and thirty-two persons the levy; the human category remains explicit.
Moses gives this portion set apart unto God to Eleazar as commanded, retaining both recipient and dedication.
The congregation's separated half introduces a second, fully retained enumeration.
The congregation receives three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep, matching the other half.
Its cattle half is thirty-six thousand, matching the earlier half without omitting the repeated number.
Its donkey half is thirty thousand five hundred, preserving the second enumeration.
Its human half is sixteen thousand, completing the four quantities before the levy statement.
Moses takes one in fifty from this half for the Levites who keep the Tent's charges, as commanded; no unstated computed totals enter the translation.
All appointed commanders of thousands and hundreds approach Moses; both ranks remain explicit.
The officers report that not even one warrior is missing after their count, preserving the emphatic negative.
Each man's found gold becomes a gift for atonement, with all five ornament categories retained.
column3: The exact material identification of the arm, wrist and hair ornaments needs specialist lexical review; the list is not collapsed to jewelry.

column2: Moses and Eleazar receive the gold, every article worked by hand; both receivers and workmanship remain.
The officers' dedicated gold totals sixteen thousand seven hundred fifty shekels, with both command ranks repeated.
Each warrior's personal plunder remains separately stated, without merging it into the officers' gift.
Moses and Eleazar bring the officers' gold into the Tent of Testimony as Israel's memorial before the Lord.
